newsitem.title: USA: Group sues hair dye maker, demands lead warnings.
newsitem.headline: Group sues hair dye maker, demands lead warnings.

text.p: An environmental group said it sued the manufacturer of Grecian Formula hair dyes on Friday, demanding warnings to consumers in California about lead in the products.

The Center for Environmental Health sued Combe Inc., which is privately held, in San Francisco Superior Court, seeking an injunction prohibiting the sale of its hair dyes in California without proper warnings.
Combe manufactures Grecian Formula and several other popular hair dyes for grey hair.
The Center for Environmental Health said several brands of Grecian Formula hair dye contain lead, which has been linked to brain damage, birth defects and cancer.
The suit was filed under the provisions of California's Proposition 65, which requires consumer warnings when toxic chemical exposure exceeds safety standards.
Combe, based in White Plains, New York, said in a statement that the lawsuit was without merit and that "no California Proposition 65 warning is necessary."
"Consumers can be assured of safety when they use Grecian Formula," Combe said, adding that clinical studies had proven the product's safety.
